content: In this paper, we present our work to support editors in the e-book annotation process. Specifically, we aim to provide tag recommendations that incorporate both the vocabulary of the editors and e-book readers. Therefore, we train various configurations of tag recommender approaches on editors' tags and Amazon search terms and evaluate them on a dataset containing Amazon review keywords. We find that combining both data sources enhances the quality of tag recommendations for annotating e-books. Furthermore, while approaches that train only on Amazon search terms provide poor performance concerning recommendation accuracy, we show that they still offer helpful annotations concerning recommendation diversity as well as our novel semantic similarity metric.
